title: Stop a faster photoelectron
hook: Change maximum electron kinetic energy and predict stopping-potential magnitude.
misconception: stopping-potential magnitude stays fixed when maximum electron kinetic energy doubles.
objective: Apply abs(V_stop) = K_max/e to compare stopping-potential magnitude when maximum electron kinetic energy changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal photoelectric stopping measurement with fixed elementary charge, abs(V_stop) = K_max/e. When maximum electron kinetic energy doubles, stopping-potential magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model abs(V_stop) = K_max/e; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal photoelectric stopping measurement with fixed elementary charge, with a nonzero initial result. If maximum electron kinetic energy triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on stopping-potential magnitude?
recall.why: Apply abs(V_stop) = K_max/e under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
